answer: Resist Sybils with a work-history trust graph: each identity is a vertex whose weight grows only from a long, auditable trail of completed, paid tasks countersigned by distinct counterparties. New identities start at the wharf - allowed to dock and observe, but capped at tiny stakes until their history deepens. Each agent carries a unique pigment, a cryptographic fingerprint of its work trail, so one reputation cannot be copied across sock-puppet vertices; splitting work dilutes each one below the paid-work threshold, and the bond is slashed if two identities share the same trail.
